zh: 5. 伊斯兰哲学
en: 5. Islamic Philosophy

zh: 在缺乏革命性替代方案的情况下，奴隶社会的瓦解导致欧洲文化遭遇了可怕的崩溃，其影响持续了几个世纪。在被称为“黑暗时代”的时期，古代的科学和艺术成就大多失传了。知识的火种在拜占庭、爱尔兰，尤其是伊斯兰世界得以延续。欧洲的大部分地区则长期深陷野蛮状态。
en: In the absence of a revolutionary alternative, the breakdown of slave society produced a frightful collapse of culture in Europe, the effects of which lasted for centuries. In the period known as the Dark Ages, the scientific and artistic achievements of Antiquity were largely lost. The flame of learning was kept alight in Byzantium, Ireland and, above all, in the Islamic world. The majority of Europe remained sunk in barbarism for a long time.

zh: 伊斯兰教诞生于公元7 世纪的阿拉伯半岛，当时阿拉伯民族正处于从原始公社制度向阶级社会过渡的时期。它标志着阿拉伯人团结在一个共同的国家（哈里发国）之下。伊斯兰教的出现从根本上改变了数百万人的生活。在希吉拉时期（公元622 年穆罕默德迁往麦地那），东罗马帝国和萨珊波斯正处于危机之中，经受了数世纪的冲突而疲惫不堪，其受压迫的臣民则在沉重的税负下苦不堪言。伊斯兰教以其简明、倡导平等的信息，特别引起了最贫穷、最受压迫的民众阶层的共鸣，他们将阿拉伯入侵者更多地视为解放者，而非压迫者。从其起源来看，伊斯兰教代表了一场革命运动，也是阿拉伯民族的觉醒。穆罕默德的最后几次演讲中的一次以如下话语结尾：“众人啊！请聆听我的话语并加以领会。要知道，每个穆斯林都是其他穆斯林的兄弟。你们所有人都是平等的。”
en: The religion of Islam arose in the seventh century in Arabia, in the period of the transition of the Arab people from the primitive communal system to class society. It signified the unification of the Arabs in a common state (the Caliphate). The advent of Islam radically transformed the lives of millions of people. At the time of the Hegira (Mohammed’s departure to Medina in 622 AD), the Eastern Roman Empire and Sassanid Persia were in crisis, exhausted by centuries of conflict, and their downtrodden subjects were crushed under the weight of taxation. With its simple, levelling message, it struck a responsive note especially among the poorest and most downtrodden layers of the population, who greeted the Arab invaders more as liberators than oppressors. In its origins, Islam represented a revolutionary movement and the awakening of the Arab nation. One of Mohammed’s last speeches ends with the following words: “Ye people! hearken to my speech and comprehend the same. Know that every Moslem is the brother of every other Moslem. All of you are of the same equality.”

zh: 与四、五世纪的哥特人入侵颇为相似，早期的阿拉伯征服运动摧毁了帝国那腐朽的体制。但与哥特人不同——哥特人征服了一个正在瓦解且以农业为主的经济体，阿拉伯人则接管了罗马帝国最富庶的行省，包括亚历山大和安提阿这两座宏伟的大都市。这在新成立的帝国范围内引发了一场深刻的精神与思想觉醒，穆斯林征服者自身也不例外。尽管后来的所谓“原教旨主义者”屡屡试图以狭隘而狂热的精神来诠释伊斯兰教，否定独立思考和文化探索，但在其早期，伊斯兰革命却为文化、艺术和哲学注入了强劲的动力。赛义德·阿米尔·阿里在其经典著作《撒拉逊人简史》中，对先知的侄子、第一个阿拉伯共和国的领袖阿里有如下评价：
en: Not unlike the Gothic invasions of the fourth and fifth centuries, the early Arab conquests swept away the rotten edifice of the imperial state. But unlike the Goths, who conquered a disintegrating and overwhelmingly rural economy, the Arabs took possession of the richest provinces of the Roman Empire, including the magnificent metropolises of Alexandria and Antioch. This produced a profound spiritual and intellectual awakening across this newly-formed empire, not least among the Muslim conquerors themselves. Despite frequent attempts by later so-called fundamentalists to interpret Islam in a narrow and fanatical spirit that denies independent thought and cultural inquiry, in its early period, the Islamic revolution gave a powerful impulse to culture, art and philosophy. In his classic Short History of the Saracens, Syed Ameer Ali has this to say about Ali, the nephew of the Prophet and head of the first Arab Republic:
body.review: 原文在此将阿里称为先知的“nephew”（侄子），译文照录这一亲属称谓，未作静默订正。

zh: 当伊斯兰教……在遥远之地扩展其影响力时，阿里正在麦地那努力引导撒拉逊民族新涌现的活力。在麦地那的公共清真寺里，阿里和他堂亲、阿巴伊斯之子阿卜杜拉讲授哲学、逻辑学、圣训（历史）、修辞学和法学，而其他人则讲授其他科目。由此形成了那场知识运动的核心，该运动在后来的巴格达展现出了巨大的力量。
en: While Islam was … extending its sway in distant parts, Ali was endeavouring in Medina to give a turn to the new-developed energy of the Saracen race. In the public mosque at Medina, Ali and his cousin, Abdullah the son of Abbais, delivered lectures on philosophy and logic, the traditions (history), rhetoric and law, whilst others dealt with other subjects. Thus was formed the nucleus of that intellectual movement which displayed itself in such great force in later times in Baghdad.

zh: 早在七世纪，情况便是如此。与现代原教旨主义者的观点相反，伊斯兰教在其起源之初，绝非对无知和狭隘狂热的崇拜。与中世纪欧洲大学中所谓“哲学”——其完全屈从于天主教会——截然不同，伊斯兰哲学并非神学的附庸。伊斯兰哲学的形成期始于八世纪末，延续至九世纪中叶。在哈里发（尤其是马蒙）的支持下，它以宽容和科学探究的自由而著称。来自被阿拉伯人征服的各国的学者，都受到国家资助的学术机构的欢迎。人们鼓励自由开放的理性主义辩论。一个重要特征是研究希腊文本的译本。当欧洲沉溺于黑暗时代之时，文化与文明的火炬在伊斯兰国家依然熠熠生辉。巴格达是这一浩瀚文明的中心，其版图从西班牙的科尔多瓦延伸至印度。
en: This was already the state of affairs in the seventh century. Contrary to the opinions of the modern fundamentalists, Islam, in its origins, was not equivalent to the worship of ignorance and narrow-minded fanaticism. In complete contrast to what passed for philosophy in the universities of medieval Europe, where it was utterly subservient to the Catholic Church, Islamic philosophy was not a handmaid of theology. The formative period of Islamic philosophy dates from the late eighth century to the mid-ninth century. Supported by the Caliphs, notably Ma’mun, it was known for its tolerance and freedom of scientific inquiry. Scholars from nations conquered by the Arabs were welcomed by state-endowed institutions. Free-ranging rationalist debate was encouraged. An important feature was the study of Greek texts in translation. At a time when Europe languished in the dark ages, the flame of culture and civilisation was kept shining brightly in the Islamic countries. Baghdad was the centre of a vast civilisation that extended from Cordoba in Spain to India.

zh: 这确实是一种具有普遍性的文明。例如，生活在中亚重要大学城布哈拉的伊斯兰思想家伊本·西那（在西方以拉丁名阿维森纳闻名），他不仅是一位哲学家，还是一位医生和自然科学家。尽管他虔诚地信奉伊斯兰教，却为将古希腊的科学与哲学知识传播至整个阿拉伯世界，进而传入欧洲做出了巨大贡献。尽管欧洲对伊斯兰教心存畏惧，却仍将阿拉伯人视为知识与教育的源泉。还有许多其他伟大的思想家，例如法拉比（活跃于9 世纪末至10 世纪初），他是伊斯兰教背景下首批政治哲学著作（《幸福的获得》和《政治体制》）的作者。伊本·西那及其同类人物帮助巩固了理性主义思想，并传播了自然科学和数学——阿拉伯人在这两个领域都取得了重大发现。
en: This was a truly universal civilisation. Islamic thinkers such as Ibn Sina (known in the West by his Latin name Avicenna), who lived in Central Asia, in the important university town of Bokhara, was not only a philosopher but also a physician and natural scientist. Although faithful to Islam, he did much to spread the knowledge of the scientific and philosophical knowledge of Greek antiquity throughout the Arab world, and thence to Europe, which, for all its fear of Islam, looked to the Arabs as a source of knowledge and education. There were many other great thinkers, like Al-Farabi (who flourished in the late ninth and early tenth centuries), the author of the first works of political philosophy within the context of the religion of Islam (The Attainment of Happiness and The Political Regime). Ibn Sina and others like him helped to consolidate rationalist thinking and propagate natural science and mathematics – both fields in which the Arabs made great discoveries.

zh: 西班牙与阿拉伯人
en: SPAIN AND THE ARABS

zh: 公元711 年开始的西班牙征服标志着世界历史的转折点。最初从北非入侵的阿拉伯人原本只打算进行一次掠夺性突袭，但西哥特王国内部的腐朽导致其迅速崩溃。阿拉伯人——或者摩尔人，正如西班牙人所称——征服了几乎整个伊比利亚半岛，并深入法国境内。征服速度之快，主要归因于受压迫的西班牙民众纷纷投奔入侵者，因为入侵者对待他们的确比那些同为基督徒的地主要好得多。
en: The conquest of Spain which began in 711 AD marked a turning-point in world history. The Arabs who made the first incursions from North Africa had only intended to make a plundering raid, but the inner rottenness of the Visigoth kingdom led to its speedy collapse. The Arabs – or Moors, as the Spaniards called them – conquered almost the whole peninsula and advanced deep into France. The speed of the conquest was mainly because the oppressed Spanish masses rallied to the invaders, who certainly treated them better than their fellow Christian landlords.

zh: 在西班牙农奴眼中，阿拉伯人并非外来征服者，而是社会解放者。他们废除了有产阶级——即封建地主和神职人员——的压迫性特权，并将沉重的税负替换为一项单一税种，该税不仅相对较轻，而且妇女、儿童、病人、盲人、乞丐或奴隶均免于缴纳。就连基督教修道院也享有免税待遇。大多数西班牙城市都获得了优待条款，而征服者也恪守了这些承诺。唯一被没收的土地，是那些逃亡投靠敌人的贵族和神职人员的土地。
en: The Arabs appeared before the Spanish serfs as social emancipators, not foreign conquerors. They abolished the oppressive rights of the possessing classes – the feudal landlords and clergy – and replaced the crushing burden of taxes by a single tax which, as well as being relatively light, was not levied on women, children, the sick, the blind, beggars or slaves. Even the Christian monasteries were exempt. Most Spanish cities were granted favourable terms which were honourably kept by the conquerors. The only land that was confiscated was that of the nobles and clergy who had fled to join the enemy.

zh: 本质上，伊斯兰教蕴含着一种民主和平等的理念，主张无论种族或肤色，所有人都应平等。对于所讨论的那个时代而言，这可谓极为先进。西班牙的阿拉伯人非但没有迫害其他信仰，反而比阿拉伯统治前后时期的基督徒都要宽容得多。他们保护所有宗教，并立即允许遭受迫害的犹太人自由礼拜。让我们回顾一下，后来西班牙宗教裁判所曾残酷地将犹太人驱逐出西班牙。与印度的莫卧儿统治者一样，他们鼓励征服者与被征服者通婚，以促进两个民族的融合。他们发展农业，并在格拉纳达、科尔多瓦和塞维利亚创造了建筑奇迹。难怪西班牙的大部分人口皈依了伊斯兰教，并通过与北方基督教封建反动势力作战，捍卫自己的家园和自由，以此表明他们的忠诚。
en: In essence, Islam contains a democratic and levelling idea which asserts the equality of all men, irrespective of race or colour. This was remarkably advanced for the period under consideration. Far from persecuting other faiths, the Arabs in Spain were far more tolerant than the Christians either before or after Arab rule. They protected all religions and immediately allowed the persecuted Jews to worship freely. Let us recall that the Spanish Inquisition later brutally expelled the Jews from Spain. Like the Mogul rulers of India, they encouraged intermarriage between the conquerors and the conquered in order to bring about the fusion of the two peoples. They advanced agriculture and created the architectural wonders of Granada, Cordoba and Seville. No wonder a large part of the Spanish population became converts to Islam, and demonstrated their loyalty by fighting to defend their homeland and freedoms against the armies of Christian-feudal reaction in the North.

zh: W. C. 阿特金森引用科尔多瓦的阿尔瓦罗那段著名的哀叹，描述伊斯兰文化对西班牙人思想的影响：
en: W. C. Atkinson describes the impact of Islamic culture on the minds of the Spaniards in the words of the famous lament of Alvaro of Cordoba:

zh: 唉，所有因才华而闻名的基督教青年，只通晓阿拉伯人的语言和文学；他们热忱地阅读和研习阿拉伯书籍，不惜重金建立起庞大的图书馆，并四处高声宣扬这种文学值得钦佩。
en: Alas, all the Christian youths who become famous for their talent know only the language and the literature of the Arabs; they read and study zealously Arabic books, of which by dint of great expenditure they form extensive libraries, and proclaim aloud on all sides that this literature is worthy of admiration.

zh: 同一位作者概述了阿拉伯人在西班牙取得的经济进步：
en: The same author outlines the economic advance achieved by the Arabs in Spain:

zh: 灌溉工程——其遗迹至今仍存——使大片降雨不规律或不足的地区变得肥沃；水稻、甘蔗及其他外来作物被引进；尽管《古兰经》禁止饮酒，但葡萄仍被大规模种植。
工业也获得了与之相媲美的繁荣，涵盖了金银开采、羊毛和丝绸织造、造纸（由阿拉伯人传入欧洲）以及九世纪在科尔多瓦发明的玻璃制造，此外还有金属加工、陶瓷和皮革制品。这些产品的声誉远播四方，为应对由此带来的繁荣贸易，一支以塞维利亚、马拉加和阿尔梅里亚为主要基地的庞大商船队应运而生。
en: Irrigation works, of which traces still survive today, made fertile wide areas of irregular or inadequate rainfall; rice, the sugar-cane, and other exotic crops were introduced; and although the Koran forbade the drinking of wine, the vine was cultivated on a large scale.

Industry enjoyed a parallel prosperity, that ranged through gold and silver mining, the weaving of wool and silk, the manufacture of paper, introduced into Europe by the Arabs, and of glass, invented in Cordoba in the ninth century, metalwork, ceramics, and leatherware. The fame of these products travelled far, and to handle the flourishing commerce that resulted there grew up a great trading fleet based chiefly in Seville, Malaga, and Almeria.

zh: 由此开启了一个持续数个世纪的经济和社会进步时期，同时也翻开了人类文化、艺术和科学史上辉煌的一章。一位评论家写道：
en: Thus began a period of economic and social advance that lasted for centuries, and with it a brilliant chapter in the history of human culture, art and science. One commentator writes:

zh: 摩尔人建立了那座令人惊叹的科尔多瓦王国，它是中世纪的奇迹；当整个欧洲都深陷于野蛮无知与纷争之中，唯有他们将知识与文明的火炬高举，在西方世界前熠熠生辉。
en: The Moors organised that wonderful kingdom of Cordova, which was the marvel of the Middle Ages, and, when all Europe was plunged in barbaric ignorance and strife, alone held the torch of learning and civilisation bright and shining before the Western world.

zh: 今天，任何人只要参观一下格拉纳达的阿尔罕布拉宫或科尔多瓦的大清真寺，就会立刻明白，西班牙的阿拉伯人远远领先于中世纪的欧洲，不仅在科学技术方面，而且在美术、雕塑和绘画方面都远胜于中世纪的欧洲。阿拉伯人的文化传统十分广泛：其中包括逻辑学、自然科学（包括心理学和生物学）、数学科学（包括音乐和天文学）、形而上学、伦理学以及政治学。无论城镇规模多小，都至少有一所学校或学院；而每个主要城镇都拥有自己的大学，包括科尔多瓦（在整个欧洲享有盛誉）、塞维利亚（伊什比利亚）、马拉加、萨拉戈萨、里斯本（阿利什布纳）、哈恩和萨拉曼卡——后者后来成为了西班牙所有大学中声望最高的学府。当时涌现出众多杰出的作家、诗人、历史学家和哲学家。
en: Anyone who today visits the Alhambra in Granada or the Mosque at Cordoba will instantly understand that the Arabs of Spain were far in advance of medieval Europe, over which they excelled, not only in science and technology, but also in the fine arts, sculpture and painting. The Arabs’ cultural tradition was broad: it included the study of logic, the sciences of nature (including psychology and biology), the mathematical sciences (including music and astronomy), metaphysics, ethics, and politics. No town, however small, was without a school or college, while every principal town had its own university, including Cordoba (renowned throughout Europe), Seville (Ishbilia), Malaga, Zaragoza, Lisbon (Alishbuna), Jaen and Salamanca, which subsequently became the most prestigious of all Spanish universities. There were a galaxy of writers, poets, historians and philosophers.

zh: 与人们的预期相反，当时有许多著名的女性知识分子。在基督教欧洲将“女性平等”视为禁忌的时代，科尔多瓦和格拉纳达却有许多杰出的女诗人和有教养的女士备受推崇。诗人阿布·侯赛因之女哈萨娜·塔米米耶和乌姆·乌拉，均出生于瓜达拉哈拉，在希吉拉历第六世纪大放异彩。来自阿尔梅里亚省的阿姆马特·乌尔·阿齐兹（先知的后裔，因此被尊称为“阿什-沙里法”）和阿尔-古萨尼耶，都是当时学界的第一流女性学者。此外还有许多其他女性。玛丽亚姆是阿布·雅库布·阿勒-安萨里的女儿，出生于塞维利亚，她在那里教授修辞学、诗歌和文学，“这些才华，加上她的虔诚、良好的品德、美德和可亲的性格，赢得了同性的喜爱，并为她赢得了许多学生。”
en: Contrary to what one might expect, there were many famous women intellectuals. At a time when the notion of the equality of women would have been anathema in Christian Europe, many distinguished women poets and cultured ladies were held in esteem in Cordoba and Granada. Hassana at-Tamimiyeh, daughter of Abu’l Hussain the poet, and Umm ul-Ula, both natives of Guadalajara, flourished in the sixth century of the Hegira. Ammat ul-Aziz (a descendant of the Prophet, and therefore styled ash-Sharifa) and al-Ghusanieh, from the province of Almeria, were both women who were in the front rank of scholars at the time. There were many others. Mariam, daughter of Abu Yakub al-Ansari, was a native of Seville, where she taught rhetoric, poetry and literature, “which, joined to her piety, her good morals, her virtues, and amiable disposition, gained her the affection of her sex, and gave her many pupils.”

zh: 落后的欧洲与先进的亚洲
en: BACKWARD EUROPE AND ADVANCED ASIA

zh: 因此，伊斯兰思想远非仅限于神秘主义和宗教狂热，它展现出对理性主义和科学的天然倾向——在这些领域，阿拉伯人曾引领世界数个世纪之久。特别是在数学和天文学方面取得了巨大进步，在科学和技术的许多其他领域也同样如此。阿尔弗雷德·胡珀在其数学史著作中指出了这一点：
en: So, far from Islamic thought being limited to mysticism and religious fanaticism, it showed a natural inclination to rationalism and science, in which, for centuries, the Arabs led the world. Great advances were made, especially in mathematics and astronomy, but also in many other spheres of science and technology. This point is made by Alfred Hooper in his history of mathematics:

zh: 我们有很多要感谢摩尔人。他们带来了关于医学和医学知识的新理念；他们传授了更先进的金属和皮革加工方法；他们在西班牙修建了水利工程、水闸和运河；总之，他们将印度和东方的智慧带给了那个已重新陷入无知和野蛮状态的欧洲。阿拉伯人熟悉那些伟大的希腊数学家的著作——正是这些数学家在希腊那脆弱而美妙的文明被极为务实且注重功用的罗马人同化之前，开创了“希腊数学的黄金时代”；他们还将从印度人那里学到的、崭新而革命性的数字书写法引入西班牙，这种方法为我们的现代科学、工程学以及航空学铺平了道路。
en: We have much for which to thank the Moors. They introduced new ideas about medicine and medical knowledge; they taught improved methods of working in metal and leather; they built waterworks, sluices and canals in Spain; in all, they brought the wisdom of India and the East to a Europe which had sunk back into ignorance and savage ways. The Arabs were familiar with the work of the great Greek mathematicians who had built up the ‘Golden age of Greek mathematics’ before the fragile and wonderful civilisation of Greece was absorbed by the intensely practical and utilitarian Romans; they also introduced into Spain the new and revolutionary method of writing numbers that they had learned from the Hindus, a method that was to pave the way for our modern world of science and engineering and aeronautics.

zh: 整个中世纪，数学领域唯一的真正进步都来自印度人和阿拉伯人。正是他们发现了三角学。正是阿拉伯人发现了代数。这个词本身就是阿拉伯语——“al-jabr”——它与许多其他事物一样，是从西班牙传入欧洲的。阿拉伯数学家花拉子米不仅撰写了一本关于印度-阿拉伯数字系统的著作（印度人在数学发展中也发挥了至关重要的作用，而阿拉伯人正是向他们学习的），还撰写了另一本关于方程处理的著作，他将其命名为《al jabr w'al muquabalah》——即“还原与对消”。该书后来被翻译成拉丁文，从而为欧洲人所熟知。
en: Throughout the Middle Ages the only real advances in mathematics were made by the Indians and Arabs. It was they who discovered trigonometry. It was the Arabs who discovered algebra. The very word is Arabic – al-jabr – which, like so many other things, found its way into Europe from Spain. The Arab mathematician al-Khowarizmi, as well as writing a book on Hindu-Arab number systems (the Indians also played a vital role in developing mathematics, and the Arabs learned from them), wrote another book on the treatment of equations which he called al jabr w’al muquabalah – the reunion and the opposition. This was later translated into Latin and hence became accessible to Europeans.

zh: 阿尔弗雷德·胡珀评论道：
en: Alfred Hooper comments:

zh: 大约从800 年到1450 年这段被称为中世纪的时期，其特征是独立思想几乎完全停滞，这不仅瘫痪了数学的进步，也像笼罩在其他所有思想家头上那样，给欧洲数学家蒙上了一层阴影。
en: The years from about 800 to about 1450, known as the Middle Ages, were marked by an almost complete stagnation of independent thought, which paralysed mathematical progress and cast its gloom over European mathematicians as over all other thinkers.

zh: 同一位作者补充道：
en: The same author adds:

zh: 在阿拉伯人将新的数字符号引入欧洲数个世纪后，许多人仍然固守着熟悉的老式罗马数字，对新系统敬而远之，因为他们将新系统与商人和异教徒联系在一起。然而到了十三世纪，这种新的数字书写系统已在欧洲各地确立。直到那时，我们如今称为“初等算术”的计算方法才得以真正发展。
en: Centuries after the Arabs had introduced the new number-symbols into Europe many people still clung to the old familiar Roman numerals and would have nothing to do with the new system, which they associated with traders and heathens. By the thirteenth century, however, the new system of writing numbers had become established in various parts of Europe. It was not until then that any real development in the number-reckoning we now call elementary arithmetic could take place.

zh: 中世纪世界主要是通过阿拉伯渠道接触到亚里士多德和柏拉图的思想。在众多对中世纪欧洲产生影响的杰出思想家中，最杰出的是伊本·鲁什德·穆罕默德，西方人称其拉丁名阿威罗伊。他是一位科学家、博学者，也是一位勇敢的激进理性主义者。这位伟大的阿拉伯哲学家生活于1126 年至1198 年间，当时正值科尔多瓦哈里发统治时期的西班牙。在他的著作中，我们可以看到源自对亚里士多德深入研读的唯物主义哲学要素。尽管他始终是一位虔诚的穆斯林，但伊本·鲁什德试图证明物质和运动既不能被创造，也不能被毁灭，从而预见了现代物理学的守恒定律。他同样否认了灵魂的不朽。
en: The Medieval world gained access to the ideas of Aristotle and Plato mainly from Arab sources. Out of a host of brilliant thinkers who influenced medieval Europe, the most outstanding was Ibn Rushd Muhammed, known in the West by his Latin name Averroes. He was a scientist, a polymath and a courageous radical rationalist. This great Arab philosopher lived between 1126 and 1198 in Spain during the Caliphate of Cordoba. In his writings, we see the elements of a materialist philosophy, derived from a careful reading of Aristotle. Although he remained a devout Muslim, Ibn Rushd attempted to prove that matter and motion could neither be created nor destroyed, thus anticipating the conservation theories of modern physics. He likewise denied the immortality of the soul.

zh: 阿威罗伊否认世界是被创造出来的。相反，他认为世界永恒地存在，且与创世神话相反，世界上从未存在过第一个人类。他一再对官方宗教的教义发起猛烈抨击，主张人类的行为不受神意支配。
en: Averroes denied that the world had been created. Rather, he held that the world had existed eternally and, contrary to the myth of genesis, that there had never been a first human. He struck blow after blow against the teachings of official religion, arguing that human acts are not ruled by divine providence.

zh: 遵循亚里士多德的观点，阿威罗伊主张知识源于感官经验；他公开将这一信念与对宗教机构和经文的盲目信仰加以对比：
en: Following Aristotle, Averroes maintained that knowledge is derived from sense experience; a belief he openly contrasted to blind faith in religious institutions and scripture:

zh: 因此，我们明确断言：每当论证的结论与经文的字面含义相冲突时，该字面含义便可依据阿拉伯语中关于此类解释的规则，进行寓意解读。这一命题未曾遭到任何穆斯林的质疑，也未曾被任何信徒所怀疑。
en: So we affirm definitely that whenever the conclusion of a demonstration is in conflict with the apparent meaning of Scripture, that apparent meaning admits of allegorical interpretation according to the rules for such interpretation in Arabic. This proposition is questioned by no Muslim and doubted by no believer.

zh: 通过采取这一立场，阿威罗伊将宗教经文降格为不应字面理解的隐喻。这公开挑战了宗教当局，而当局对阿威罗伊怀有深深的疑虑。因此，这些思想如此激进，以致他的理论不仅遭到正统穆斯林的迫害，而且正如我们稍后将看到的，也遭到了天主教会的迫害。阿威罗伊著作的影响力和重要性不容低估。正是主要通过这位杰出哲学家的著作——尤其是他对亚里士多德的注释——欧洲人才最初得以接触到那个早已被遗忘的古典希腊哲学世界。
en: By taking this position, Averroes relegated religious scripture to mere metaphors which should not be taken literally. This was an open attack on the religious officialdom who looked at Averroes with suspicion. So radical were these ideas, that his theories were persecuted by orthodox Muslims, and, as we shall see later, also by the Catholic church. The influence and importance of Averroes’ works cannot be underestimated. It was primarily through the work of this remarkable philosopher, particularly his commentaries on Aristotle, that Europeans initially became acquainted with the long-forgotten world of classical Greek philosophy.

zh: 这一知识的主要源泉是伊斯兰西班牙——在被基督徒摧毁之前，那里曾是一个繁荣昌盛、文化昌明的国度。格拉纳达、塞维利亚和科尔多瓦都是举世闻名的学术重镇。所有宗教都受到开明的宽容对待——直到西班牙人，在那些目光短浅、狂热的偏执狂卡斯蒂利亚的费尔南多和阿拉贡的伊莎贝拉的带领下，着手将阿尔-安达卢斯的精华化为一堆血腥的灰烬。
en: The main fountainhead of this knowledge was Islamic Spain, which, until it was destroyed by the Christians, was a flourishing, prosperous and cultured nation. Granada, Seville and Cordoba were important and internationally renowned centres of learning. All religions were treated with enlightened tolerance – until the Spaniards, led by those narrow-minded and fanatical bigots Fernando of Castille and Isabelle of Aragon, set about reducing the flower of Al-Andalus to a heap of bloody ashes.

zh: 所谓的“十字军东征”——关于它已写下太多浪漫的废话——不过是野蛮人对在各方面都优于他们的民族所发动的无数次破坏性且嗜血的突袭罢了。一位记录格拉纳达围城战的基督教编年史家阿加皮托神父，曾用轻蔑的语气描述阿拉伯人的洗漱习惯：
en: The so-called Crusades, about which so much romantic rubbish has been written, were just so many destructive and bloodthirsty raids of barbarians against people who were, in every respect, their superiors. One of the Christian chroniclers of the siege of Granada, Father Agapito, writes in contemptuous terms about the Arab habit of washing themselves:

zh: ［对］这些异教徒而言，水比面包更不可或缺，他们将其用于可诅咒的宗教所乐见的每日反复净身，还用于沐浴以及其他千百种我们西班牙人和基督徒所不屑一顾的闲散奢靡之举。
en: [W]ater is more necessary to these infidels than bread, making use of it in repeated daily ablutions enjoyed by their damnable religion, and employing it in baths and in a thousand other idle and extravagant modes, of which we Spaniards and Christians make but little account.
body.review: 原文此处作“enjoyed by their damnable religion”（为其宗教所乐见）；底稿译作“所要求”，可能按“enjoined”理解。此处按所给英文照译。

zh: 十字军东征的反动与野蛮本质，已被斯蒂芬·朗西曼等现代历史学家充分揭示。以下是另一位作家的典型摘录：
en: The reactionary and barbarous nature of the Crusades has been sufficiently demonstrated by modern historians like Stephen Runciman. Here is a typical extract by another writer:

zh: 在每座被攻占的城市里，塔富尔人［贫穷的十字军战士］洗劫了所有能抢到手的东西，强奸穆斯林妇女，并进行肆意屠杀。十字军的正式领导人对他们完全无法管束。当安提阿埃米尔就塔富尔人的食人行径提出抗议时，诸位亲王只能歉疚地承认：“我们所有人联合起来，也无法驯服塔富尔国王。”
en: In each captured city the Tafurs [poor crusaders] looted everything they could lay their hands on, raped the Moslem women and carried out indiscriminate massacres. The official leaders of the Crusade had no authority over them at all. When the Emir of Antioch protested about the cannibalism of the Tafurs, the princes could only admit apologetically: “All of us together cannot tame King Tafur”.

zh: 还有：
en: And again:

zh: 耶路撒冷陷落之后，一场大屠杀随之而来；除了总督及其卫队……每一位穆斯林——无论男女老幼——都被杀害。在所罗门圣殿内及周边地区，“战马在血泊中跋涉，血深及膝，甚至及至马嚼子。同一处圣地曾长期将那些亵渎之人的罪孽呈献给上帝，如今却要承受他们的鲜血，这正是上帝公正而奇妙的审判。”至于耶路撒冷的犹太人，当他们躲进主会堂时，建筑被点燃，他们全都被活活烧死。十字军一边喜极而泣，一边唱着赞美诗，列队行进至圣墓教堂。“啊，新的一天，新的一天与欢欣，崭新而永恒的喜乐……那一天，将载入未来所有世纪的史册，将我们所有的苦难与艰辛化作了喜乐与欢欣；那一天，是基督教的巩固，是异教的覆灭，是我们信仰的复兴！”
en: The fall of Jerusalem was followed by a great massacre; except for the governor and his bodyguard … every Moslem – man, woman and child – was killed. In and around the Temple of Solomon “the horses waded in blood up to their knees, nay up to the bridle. It was a just and wonderful judgement of God that the same place should receive the blood of those whose blasphemies it had so long carried up to God.” As for the Jews of Jerusalem, when they took refuge in their chief synagogue the building was set on fire and they were all burnt alive. Weeping with joy and singing songs of praise the crusaders marched in procession to the church of the Holy Sepulchre. “O new day, new day and exultation, new and everlasting gladness… That day, famed through all centuries to come, turned all our sufferings and hardships into joy and exultation; that day, the confirmation of Christianity, the annihilation of paganism, the renewal of our faith!”

zh: 颇具讽刺意味的是，时至今日，欧洲人仍自诩为人类文化的唯一传承者，而事实上，在整个中世纪时期，他们充当的却是东方文化的掘墓人。实际上，现实情况与西方编造的神话恰恰相反。正是伊斯兰世界维系着艺术、科学和哲学的火种，当欧洲开始走出“黑暗时代”时，这些火种才逐渐传入欧洲。
en: It is ironic that, to this day, Europeans still see themselves as the exclusive bearers of human culture when for the whole of the Middle Ages they acted as the grave-diggers of culture in the East. In reality the roles were opposite to the myths created by the West. It was in the Islamic world that the flame of art, science and philosophy were kept alive and slowly found their way into Europe as it began to emerge out of the Dark Ages.
